utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours. Alex Demirdjian for the Prosecution with Belinda Pidwell and Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Appearing for Mico Stanisic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Ms. Deirdre Montgomery and Annemarie McNulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Aleksandar Aleksic and Miroslav Cuskic appearing for Stojan Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the witness comes back into court, can we go back into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And if there are no preliminary matters, may the usher please escort the witness back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bubic, good morning to you. You may resume your seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And before Mr. Demirdjian continues his cross-examination, I remind you that you are still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bubic, I would like to ask you a clarification. Yesterday, at page 25889, you said that in early 1992 you were the owner of a chain of boutiques, is that right, in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What was the name of that chain of boutique, please?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sloboda.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you remember yesterday I showed you a document dated the 8th of June, 1992, which was the appointment of Mane Tepic, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You expressed your views, I believe, that there was a problem with the document. So we did a little bit of digging around. I'd like to show you a series of five appointments in relation to your light brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we first have up number 20366, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, I want you to look at each of these five appointments, one by one, and reserve your comments for the end. Look at them as a package. So the first one on the screen -- yes. The first one on the screen should be in relation to Andjelko Stanic, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you know Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And was he a member of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, and we see that the date is 8th of June, 1992, signed by Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we have the next one which is 20367, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: 20367 is in relation to Zivko Krsic, commander for moral and guidance. Did you know Mr. Krsic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Krsic well. He was my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And it says here that he is commander for moral and guidance. On the 8th of June, he was appointed and it signed by Dusan Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we see the other one, 20368.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The next one is for Mr. Nenad Jerkovic, commander for logistics. You knew Mr. Jerkovic. You told us that yesterday, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And he is also appointed on the 8th of June, and it is signed by Mr. Dusan Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we go to 20369, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Novakovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, 20369 is in relation to Slavica Jerosimovic, chief of quartermaster service, and he, too, is appointed on the 8th of June, 1992, and is it signed by Dusan Novakovic. Did you know Jerosimovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs., I knew her by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the last one is 20370. And 20370 is in relation to a man by the name of Zeljko Tesic, chief of the medical service. Do you know Mr. Tesic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is a physician and still works in Kotor Varos. He has his private practice there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right. So, sir, yesterday you suggested that there was an error with the appointment of Mr. Tepic. I put it to you that, in fact, these documents are all correct. You simply were not involved in the creation process of these appointments. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I'm not contesting the correctness of these documents. What I'm saying is that I'm not aware of them. I don't know anything about them. As far as I know, the brigade on that date was not established yet. This is what I know. This is my personal knowledge because I met Commander Novakovic only when I was released from prison. I had never met him before I was taken prisoner. So it doesn't make too much sense to me. Maybe this did happen on the 8th of June, I'm not denying even that, but maybe that was done for some future period, for something that would be done with a delay. In any case, this is something that I'm absolutely not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday that you too were mobilised on the 8th of June; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th or on 9th I said. I believe that it was on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that the series of these five appointments -- yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Demirdjian. I had thought that the issue was the stamp, and so my question goes to the witness: If you can recognise the number on the stamp, because I notice that on each of the documents that we've just seen the stamp carries the same number, and I think it was your suggestion yesterday that this number did not belong to the unit that you knew.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So now what?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask for the witness to remove his headphones for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bubic, can you take off your headphones, just for a seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we did some backgrounds checks and it may be that we'll been in a position to address this with the witness who has a bit more knowledge about military issues, if there is any occasion in the near future. Our information is that this is an old JNA stamp, and, indeed, as the witness indicated yesterday the new stamps bore a four-digit code starting with 7. The one we saw yesterday was 7001, I believe. We do have other documents showing stamps later on in 1992 of this brigade when it changed, but our information is this is an old JNA stamp with a five-digit code. So at this stage what I'm proposing to do is to tender the appointment of Mr. Tepic who is the commander of his brigade, the one that I showed yesterday, along with these five appointments. The point being that this witness is being called to talk about the activities of his brigade and his evaluation of the numbers of armed forces of the other side and we are saying that these documents go to his credibility. He is too much of a low-level witness. He does not know exactly the composition of his own command, of his own brigade. And, in fact, second point is this document shows that a number of people were appointed a few days before the take-over in Kotor Varos and that this brigade was being formed during the month of June, and, indeed, it was established that as we saw from documents in the month of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just ask the Defence if there's any issue from your side regarding the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as you have said it yourself, I notice that the stamp is the same on the six or seven documents and that the number of the decision in the heading is also the same. My objection with regard to the -- today's part of the cross-examination by the Prosecutor is this: He asked the witness whether he is familiar with these people and whether they were members of the brigade, and the witness confirmed all that. And I'm not contesting that. However, my learned friend from the Prosecution did not clarify with the witness whether the witness knew that all those persons, all those individuals on the 8th of June started discharging duties to which they were appointed according to these decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We asked the witness to remove his headphones, but clearly he can understand what is being said right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Really, that was not my intention. You are absolutely right. I agree that my learned friend can use this line of questioning in order to challenge the witness's credibility. However, he explained yesterday what he knew and what he thought about the documents shown to him yesterday. However, as for today's set of documents, the Prosecutor has not exactly clarified what I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- we see the logic in your application in terms of the document from yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- ignoring for the moment the illogicality of the witness not being able to speak to it from his own knowledge, but we see the purpose for which you wish to tender that, but we don't see why these additional documents need similarly to come in. It seems to us that the point that you are making would be adequately made by allowing the -- yesterday's document in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honours. I agree. So if we just tender 65 ter 20340, that should suffice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So that's -- that document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2418, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And the witness may replace his head phones.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I may be mistaken, but I believe that the document that was shown to the witness yesterday was not admitted into evidence, at all, yesterday on the appointment of Mane Tepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's what we were doing right now. Yes, that's what just happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, could we also have up 65 ter 20348, which was the list I showed you yesterday, tab 39. Do you remember this list that I showed you yesterday, sir, which had members of your unit. You named two men, Asim Aganbegovic and Adis Hadziselimovic, as members of the Croat and Muslim community who remained in the TO and later on the VRS. Now, let me ask you, before coming to court yesterday, had you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Because you told us that you spent a number of days in proofing with Mr. Aleksic. Was this document not shown to you at all?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the document wasn't shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If you look at the far right, you see the ethnicity of the commanding officers of this unit. They are all Serbs on the first page. If you go to the second page, it also says Serbian for every one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we can go to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It all says Serbian. They are all Serbs. And if we go to the last page, page 3 in the B/C/S version, we see two who are not marked as Serbs. And these are the very two same persons that you named yesterday. One is marked as a Yugoslav and one actually does not even have an ethnic -- and then ethnicity. So there are 57 names on this list and only two of them are not Serbs, and these are the same two that you told us yesterday. So are you sure you've never seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, yesterday you also told us that in the reserve police there were quite a few Muslims and Croats who remained after the take-over; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you gave us two names and you say you were not able to give us any other names. In your view, how many Muslims and Croats remained in the reserve police? You don't have to give us a precise number.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise number because I don't know it, but I believe that there were four or five Muslims, approximately, and slightly fewer Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you know, ballpark figure, how many reserve police officers were there in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If I told you that there was 265 reserve police officers in Kotor Varos, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with you because I don't know. I can't agree with something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Moreover, that number sounds a bit exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, yesterday, you told us at page 25925 that during your captivity Sprzo told you that on the left bank of the Vrbanja there's more than 1.000 of them. When you meant "of them," you meant of non-Serb forces, and you added that you really doubted that number. Do you remember telling us in that in court yesterday?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I thought that they tried to daunt me with bragging about their forces, because objectively I had not encountered that many of them, but where I was, in the places where I was -- which means I was not along the entire length of the bank of the river that was controlled by the Muslim forces, but in the places where I was and where I was passing through, I must have seen over 200 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, it is an accepted fact in this case that on the day of the take-over - the take-over took place, in fact, on the 11th of June - and that this take-over took place without any resistance; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was the case. It is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you told us that you were guarding buildings throughout the month of June. Was guarding buildings your only assignment, sir?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my only assignment, my exclusive assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us which buildings were you guarding exactly?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the Bregovi neighbourhood in front of high-rise building called Kocka 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the Bregovi neighbourhood, what is the distance between this neighbourhood and the centre of Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I'm the best person to ask that question. There's some 500 metres between the general assembly building and the very centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this Kocka 1, 2 and 3, what are these buildings exactly? What were you guarding exactly?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our task was not to allow the population to go out of the buildings and we were to make sure that nobody used any weapons and killed anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So these are apartment buildings?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And what were you wearing when you were guarding these buildings?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wore a grey, olive uniform of the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when you say that you wanted to ensure that nobody got out of the buildings, were you, in fact, enforcing the curfew?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no curfew yet, but the people in the command of the town defence told us to guard these buildings, to make sure nobody ventured out as there was also a threat of sniper fire. There was some soldiers moving about as well from the 22nd Brigade. Therefore, there was always a possibility of somebody producing an incident. There were a lot of intoxicated people, and it was best to make sure that nobody was out in the street and that the people were safely in their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What kind of a weapon did you have on you while you were guarding?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, sir, could you tell us, prior to the take-over, who was the secretary for national defence in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aforementioned Mane Tepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you know a man by the name of Miro Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Miro Petrusic in person. However, he was present in the police station building, the same building that housed the national defence department. He was there for a short while, but I can't really tell you what he was doing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, it is, in fact, that Mr. Petrusic arrived late, in fact, early in 1992. Did you know that he was the secretary for national defence in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he worked there but I didn't know what his duties were because I don't know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know the chairman of the national defence council, Anto Mandic? Did you know of him?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know of him. He was the president of the municipality of Kotor Varos up until the 11th of June. I had never had any dealings with him, so I didn't know him personally. I knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And did you know the SJB commander, Nedjeljko Maric, or did you know of him?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also knew him by sight. I used to see him around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Petrusic, Mr. Mandic and Mr. Maric were arrested on the 11th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't really matter, but I did hear of it at a later date. I can't remember exactly when. I also knew -- no, no, no, no, I'm mistaken. That's not him. I can't recall the name at this time. No, no, it was Sadikovic I had in mind. No, I was mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. These three men you said you heard later on that they were arrested, did you also hear they were beaten black and blue once they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine. You told us yesterday that during the month of June and July, there were negotiations for the surrender of weapons. And that these negotiations were conducted with religious officials, hodzas and Catholic priests. For reference it's page 25906. So effectively, sir, your forces arrested the head of the National Defence, the SJB commander and the head of the executive -- well, the chairman of the National Council as well. The three leading figures of the non-Serb community who, prior to the take-over, held key positions in Kotor Varos. And then what you are telling us is that your forces were expecting to negotiate with religious officials. Was that the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can you just repeat what you just said, sir. Interpreters didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not hearing the interpretation well. I'm having trouble with my headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we check that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's fine. It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you need me to repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's okay. Yes, yes, please, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you told us about negotiations yesterday, during the months of June and July. And you said that these negotiations were conducted with religious priests, hodzas, and Catholic priests; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among them were also certain citizens of more prominence who were -- who had some sort of authority among the people. There were also representatives of the army. There was also Zdravko Pejic, who was involved in negotiations and he performed certain duties for the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We understand. But what I'm putting to you is that on the non-Serb side, you had arrested all the key figures of the civilian authorities. You had arrested the head of the National Council, the SJB commander, and the chairman the National Council, the three people we mentioned earlier today, and what you are doing is you are negotiating with religious officials. Wasn't that the situation?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the religious officials who negotiations were held with, rather, it was the religious officials and citizens of renown who went to the various villages to conduct these negotiations with the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I will not belabour the point. Sir, you were aware that non-Serb civilians were arrested on the day of the take-over?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you fully. I do know, or rather, I heard that a surrender of weapons operation was launched and those who refused to surrender weapons were brought in for interviews. That's all I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your position is that anyone who did not have a weapon or who did surrender was not arrested?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do not know of a single individual who would have been arrested in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you don't know of any women or elderly men who were arrested either?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, during the month of June, these arrests were conducted by the police and the army. Do you remember seeing the Special Police from Banja Luka during the take-over on the 11th of June?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We ordinary citizens referred to all those policemen who we didn't know and who wore camouflage uniforms as specials. It was a novelty of sorts to see troops in camouflage uniforms. There had been no camouflage uniforms worn by soldiers previously. As for policemen, I wouldn't say that it was a camouflage uniform. It was, perhaps, a version of their blue uniform. So people would refer to all such individuals wearing that sort of uniform as specials. So any expertise I might have in that respect is quite lacking, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you were telling us just before that you were guarding the buildings that you mentioned during this month. Did you see -- did you know that there was a Catholic church close to your building, the Kocka 1, 2, and 3?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. It is in the immediate vicinity of the apartment building where I lived -- or live, maybe some 30 or 40 metres away. And even -- I am sorry, I even took part in building the church. I gave a personal contribution for this church to be constructed. As a neighbour and acquaintance, I was on quite good terms with the priest who was serving there by the name of Mato or Franjo, I can't remember. I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, were you there when it burned down on the 2nd of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was this right next to the building that you were guarding?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I don't know where I was on that day. What I do know is that when I returned in the afternoon hours, the church was still alight. Stories circulated that the Serbs set fire to it, and then I heard other stories that the Croats set it alight so that the Serbs may not use it for whatever purposes they see -- saw fit. So I don't know to this day who is responsible for the destruction of that church. The only thing I know is that the church was reconstructed. It was rebuilt, and it looks just the same as it did before the war and I'm really glad about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And in which year was it rebuilt?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the construction works ended some two or three years ago, and people from all quarters gather there for various Catholic festivities, and there's always a crowd of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, when you were telling us of your -- the day that you were captured on the 5th of July, you told us that after the funeral you were in Vrbanjci at the command. Can you clarify for us that it was the command of which unit exactly?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. I wasn't in the command. I was outside of it in front of a cafe --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The command itself --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not the same thing, really, is it, to be in the command or outside of it? There was a catering establishment. Let me be quite clear, I never stepped foot into that catering establishment, either before the war or after the war, and I really don't know what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. It was a probably mistake in my question, and that is not the point. The point I'm asking you right now is: Which unit was stationed at that command?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the command of the 22nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And this brigade also had a command post, you told us, in Maslovare, I believe?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was in the early days, but then, and perhaps I may be mistaken in that, they either relocated the entire command from Maslovare or part of it, so we referred to that cafe as the command of the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, while the unit was in Maslovare, when it arrived, did you know that the commander of the unit stationed in Maslovare was Slobodan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of one battalion only at the start when they got there first. Allegedly, the 22nd, when it arrived, had the strength of a battalion. I don't know where other battalions were, if there were any. What I do know is that together with Slobodan, there was Mr. Peulic there as well. He was the commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you know what, if any, relationship did Mr. Slobodan Zupljanin have with Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are related. Three times removed, I think. I think their grandfathers were brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Moving back to Vrbanjci, now, it is correct to say that by the 5th of July when you were outside, not in the command post, by this time Vrbanjci had been attacked by the Serb forces about ten days prior to that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's difficult for me to say now truly whom attacked whom, since the Muslims were on the left bank of the Vrbanja and opened fire on to the population on the right bank. And it was mixed population. In the very centre there was Serbs and Muslims, and a bit further uphill there were Croats living. Based on what I heard, and it was stories in the grape-vine, after several failed attempts at holding talks, a unit set out from within the 22nd Brigade supported by the Kotor police - well, at any rate, from the municipality, I don't know exactly where, with weapons, and I did mention it yesterday - and it was at that point that our forces in the area sustained major casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, 50 civilians, non-Serb civilians, were killed on an attack on the 25th of June, 1992. Do you say that this did not happen?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 25th of June?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: 25th of June there was an attack on Vrbanjci by Serb forces. You are telling us you heard about it. You didn't take part in this attack?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I most certainly didn't take part in it. I did hear of it, though. The attacks were more or less frequent, but this is the first time I've heard of 50 people having been killed there. It's the first time. It's not that I'm denying it. It's possible. It's just that I don't know. It wasn't something I was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you did not take part in this attack? That's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You also told us that this was a mixed village. It is correct to say that was predominantly inhabited by non-Serbs; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, which village are you referring to, Vrbanjci?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Serbs, Croats, and Muslims, all of them were represented, I'm sure. It was -- well, it's a coincidence, but I am married to a lady from that village, and there's an entire street that is inhabited by Serbs. And there's an odd Croat house in that street and several others --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, the question is not if there were Serbs, Croats and Muslims. That I agree with. The question is: Were you aware that it was predominantly inhabited by non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on to the 5th of July, the event you described where Colonel Stevilovic, Markovic, and Petrusic were killed, where you were captured. Now, you told us that you didn't know Stevilovic on that day. Had you heard of him before?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You did not know what kind of activities he was involved in as part of the military intelligence of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I most certainly didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So on that day when you were in Vrbanjci, you went into the car with these two men you did not know anything about?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you didn't tell us where you started off on that day. You told us you travelled to Obudnjik for the funeral. Where were you at the beginning of the day? Were you in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in a hamlet of Rujka that I mentioned yesterday. There was a guard stationed there, in case Sadikovic's forces were to strike from the direction of Bilice. This is some 200 metres from my flat, as the crow flies. And then in the morning, I went to Maslovare and then attended the funeral and went back to Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The question was: Where were you at the beginning of the day. So to make sure we are able to finish your testimony today, I will ask you to just focus on the question, and if I need additional details, I will ask you. Can we agree on that? So, Rujika, that's in the north of Kotor Varos; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. So you travelled from Rujika all the way to Maslovare and you had to pass through Vrbanjci on your way, is that right, on the main road?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what were you wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The grey, olive JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. So just to recapture your evidence, you went from Rujika in the north of Kotor Varos, you travelled all the way to Maslovare, you went to Obudnjik for the funeral, you then went to Vrbanjci, and from Vrbanjci you ended up in Vujevica [phoen] where you were captured. Does that summarise your travel on that day?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I set out from Vrbanjci towards Kotor Varos, I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday that you asked permission the day before that, on the 4th of July, to attend the funeral, and you asked this permission -- you asked this to Gojko Stolic; right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, can we pull up 65 ter 20351, please. It's tab 45. Your Honours, since we only received this document which is, in fact, Mr. Bubic's book, we only received it last Thursday, we were unable to request a full translation so we were able to do a cursory review and manage to select some portions for translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is the cover page of your book; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we go to - this is going to get tricky - page 5 in the English version which should be page 6 in the B/C/S version. Now, to help you out, can we zoom in to page 10 on the B/C/S, the left side of the page in the B/C/S. Bottom of -- okay. That's fine. Scroll down a little bit, please. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, do you see on that page that you asked permission to Ziza or Zivko Krsic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Demirdjian kindly speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I'll repeat my question. I guess we have that question in. So, sir, do you see that you asked permission to Zivko Krsic first?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need to see this. I know this. Zivko Krsic was visiting the army at their century posts and along the way I heard from him that the funeral would take place tomorrow in Dabovci, and I told him it would bode well for me to go because they were my neighbours and along the way I would visit the family in Maslovare. He told me to come to the command, town command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Pause for a seconds. My only question was that you asked Zivo Krsic. Now, I want to take you too --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we slide to page 11 in the B/C/S version and can we scroll down to -- in the English version scroll down to the bottom of that page. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, on that page, at the bottom of your page, page 11, that Mr. Krsic warned you to not get on that road because the next day on the 5th of July at 10.00 in the morning an air attack was expected on Vecici? You see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You did not mention that yesterday, that there was an air attack on Vecici on the 5th of July. Now, despite the warning, and I understand that it's in your book, you also spoke to Mr. Stolic and you decided to get on that road?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You decided to get on that road on the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can put away the book for a second, and I would ask that we pull up P1818 which is at tab 15A.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, what I'm showing you right now is a document of the 1st Krajina Corps of the 15th of July, 1992. What I'd like you to do is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: First, we can go to the last page and see that it was signed by the Assistant Commander Vukelic. Very well. And now we can go back to page 2 in both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in your version, in the B/C/S version, just above the section called B, just above that, there is a paragraph that begins with the words "Na Vlasickom."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this document says that three surprises occurred on the Vlasic plateau resulting in of the deaths of 16 MUP and four members of the 122nd Light Infantry Brigade. There is substantial presence of HOS and Green Beret formation in that area. Now, the next sentence says that many of the casualty resulted from a lack of vigilance and the relaxed attitude of civilian police members as well as a lack of combat discipline. Individuals and groups entered the said dangerous areas on their own initiative and conducted actions there. Some of them wanted to demonstrate the courage of Krajina and were killed for this reason. Now, sir, this is exactly what happened in your case, wasn't it? You knew very well on that day that in Vujevica, and this is information that your command possessed, there were possible targets or ambushes, and you even told us that Markovic casually said that not every bullet kills. So on that day there were clear signs that this was a dangerous area and, nonetheless, your car drove through; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But I need to explain something. Since Mr. Krsic told me that planes would do some bombing that day, on the left bank of the Vrbanja river, on the right as I was travelling, I didn't see any reason to fear this bombing, supposedly the road was clear and it was a clear road. And the reason to visit my family and the funeral of these three young men, this was the reason, and it didn't require any particular courage on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically, I was not a brave soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, now, I'm going to put my next question to you and I want you to know, as I've indicated in the beginning, I do not challenge what happened to you on that day, that these three men were killed and that you were captured and you were in detention for 16 days. I do not challenge that for one minute. However, in your book, you said during your captivity you found that Sprzo's unit was receiving information from Serb informants. I believe in your book you call them "spies." And that these informants were updating Sprzo on a regular basis about the movement of senior army officers. Do you remember that in your book, or do you want me to pull it up?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I didn't write about the movements of many officers, reports of their movements, but that he told me that he knew the situation on our side very well and that there were people on our side who conveyed this to him, and that is that's correct, but not high-ranking officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you were aware that at the time after you were released there were suggestions that Colonel Stevilovic, his killing was organised by his own side? Did you hear of such suggestions at the time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear this, yes. Perhaps that was the reason to write what I wrote so that the truth would finally come out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, however, you were not part of the plotting of this killing, were you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: God forbid.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you know that Colonel Stevilovic, just five days before he was killed, was involved in an operation in Teslic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the basis of this question, please? The witness said that he met them for the first time when he went into the car. He didn't know these men beforehand. How can it be expected that the witness would know what Stevilovic meant to do five days before?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You didn't hear the rest of my question. Let me put the question first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, and this is in relation, again, to my last question which is what you heard after you were released. Did you know and did you hear that Stevilovic was involved in an operation in Teslic just five days prior to his killing, and that this operation was aimed at arresting a group of Serb soldiers and policemen known as the Mice group? Did you ever hear of this after your release?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I never, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So in those suggestions that you heard after your release, what reasons did you hear for his killing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one mentioned any reasons to me, but of all the stories that I heard -- one particular story that I heard was that Serbs killed him. Another story was that he was betrayed by the Serbs, that some of these spies had reported when he would be travelling towards Kotor Varos. The third version I heard from Sprzo while in captivity and that it wasn't meant for him, for the two of them, that they were not to be killed, that the killing was being prepared for Peulic and Zupljanin. I did believe this somewhat later when I came out of captivity. I also heard about Savo Tepic, that he was released, that he had gone through, that they didn't want to shoot at him, that they were waiting for Peulic and Slobodan Zupljanin. I even talked to Savo about this later, and I asked him why he would do this when -- I asked him if there was room for Kotor Varos and I felt very unpleasant, and at the time he said it's very dangerous and he said it was better for one person to be in the car rather than two, three, four five people. If someone dies then fewer will die. And that's what I heard later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's is fine, sir. I have one document, we have a series of them, but I'll just limit myself to one. Sir, were you aware that the funeral of Mr. Stevilovic took place the day after he was killed?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you hear about it later on?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you know that a funeral did take place which was attended by the commanding officers starting by Momir Talic and Ratko Mladic. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Since I didn't know about the funeral, I couldn't know the other information about it, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm not going to get into the details of this, but we have in evidence the war diary of the 1st Krajina Corps which shows who exactly attended this funeral. What I want to show you is a document at tab 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Which is 65 ter 20346.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm sure you are aware that the chief of your army, Mr. Mladic, was taking detailed notes during war time. I'm sure you've heard of this in the media; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about these diaries perhaps about a month ago, recently, since he has come to The Hague. And the initial knowledge I had about it was through the media, so it's quite fresh.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, as I told you, we have the war diary of the first KK which shows that Mr. Mladic attended this funeral. So he was aware on the same day that Mr. Stevilovic was killed. He was aware of this fact. Now, I want you to look at the notes he took during a meeting in 1994 with General Subotic, and what he says here two years after the event was that regarding 3 and a half kilos of gold, it seems that the late Colonel Stevilovic and Markovic knew about this, and this may have been the reason why Stevilovic died. Do you see this at the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. I see it, Subotic saying this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is two years after the events, after you were debriefed by the military police, and it appears that in 1994 even the chief of your army had doubts about who organised the killing. So, sir, I put it to you that -- and -- well, I put it to you that although Sprzo and his men did execute this operation which resulted in the killing of the three men and your captivity, his own army took part in the organisation of his death?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you are mistaken, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well, sir. So your evidence is that his own side did not organise his killing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not certain. I watched it with my own eyes, everything, and this unfortunate man, Sprzo, while I was with him there on the other side, I had come to trust him in a certain way, he would have told me this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: But he didn't tell you -- just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a second, please. In your book, he did tell you that he was receiving information from Serb insiders and information about movement of Serb officers. He did tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you show this where this is written in the book, can you read it please, where it's written about Stevilovic and Markovic as well. Furthermore, if I know that this part of General Mladic diary has been admitted, you can call him, he is in The Hague and he can tell you what he thinks. Don't take things out of context. Getting to know the effects of the Operation Granica 94, what do we know about Operation Granica 94?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You can deal with this --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you did not pose the question properly. You took it out of context. You were not fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. Demirdjian, the witness's testimony at bottom is that he doesn't really know what the background was to this, so the whereas the Prosecution may have a theory as to what happened, how does -- where does that take us in terms of evidence? The witness -- you are examining this witness. He says he doesn't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this witness was one of the victims who was arrested on that day. He was part of this event. If anything, I would expect that he would have the curiosity to know what happened, and it is in his book that there were such suggestions. That's where I was going at. And my final conclusion was to put to him that although it was organised by one side, it was executed by another. That was all I was suggesting. And Mr. Aleksic can deal with the book, if he would like to, in re-examination. But that is not the point. The point was to show him that there were suggestions out there. I was trying to explore to see if he was aware of them. That is all. That is all. So if I come back to my specific question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And it will be my last question before the break, sir. What I asked you specifically, I told you before I'm not challenging the fact that Sprzo executed the operation per se, what I'm suggesting to you was that the killing of Stevilovic, Markovic, Petrusic is not limited to the operation of Sprzo that his own army took part in organising it, preparing it, or, in any way, providing information to Sprzo and his men. Can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. One thing, during my decent captivity, I came to trust Sprzo in a certain way. He was a man to whom I opened my heart and soul, and if he told me that it was not meant for the generals, as he referred to them, that this was meant for Mr. Peulic and for Slobodan, then there is no doubt for -- reason for me to doubt him. I think he was quite sincere to me. There were moments when he was really open and sincere to me. Therefore, had the Serb side organised it and had it gone through him on his side, he would have told me - I am confident of this - but he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So how do you explain that in your book you tell us that he had information from the Serb side about the movements of Serb officers?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the third time, Mr. Demirdjian is saying something that is not written in this book. He should show this. The witness answered his question. I've read the book myself and there it says that Sprzo told the witness that he had information, that he had information about the situation in the Serbian army, the usual information. But there is no mention of the movement of officers, and the witness has said this, and now this is being repeated for the third time and it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, it appears that Mr. Cvijetic and Mr. Aleksic cannot read. Can we please go back to tab 45, please. And in e-court and in the B/C/S version -- I'll wait for it to come up. Tab 45. I apologise, 65 ter 20351. I hope I'm relying on a proper translation now. So if we go to page 25 in e-court for the B/C/S version. On the book that should be page 48. Yes. Can we zoom into the right side. And in the English version it's page 7. Scroll to the right side of that page and zoom into the top paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see the paragraph, sir, where it says: "He even said that spies were mostly Serbs who do not like Slobodan nor Peulic, and he was convinced that they were informing him correctly and on a regular basis about their movement." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness needs to read the entire paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. So does it say, and Mr. Cvijetic --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, this pertains only to information about Slobodan and Peulic. He didn't mention anyone else to me that they were following anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And Slobodan and Peulic are senior Serb officers of the army; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I think this is a good time, Your Honours, for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we talk the break to return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is being brought in, may I just extend my apologies to Mr. Aleksic and Mr. Cvijetic for the comments I made earlier. In the heat of the moment you say things that you don't necessarily mean and that I thought that that was not in my nature. So, in any event, my apologies for the comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the sake of timing, Your Honours, I shouldn't be much longer, probably another half-hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bubic, I'd like to go back to the day of the take-over on the 11th of June. We haven't explored this topic yet with you. Can you tell us exactly where you were on that day?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Performing my duty as the -- the guard for those buildings in the centre of the neighbourhood where I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And is it correct to say that these buildings were approximately 200 metres away from the Kotor Varos sawmill, give or take?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And while you were guarding your building, were you able to see civilians being brought into the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on that day. Sometime later, I did see groups of civilians coming to the sawmill. To the best of my knowledge, they were people from the nearby locations where combat activities had already begun, whether it was from this end or the other end. I heard that the better part of the population had expressed their willingness to leave Kotor Varos, so rather than having to go door to door to collect these individuals, the authorities informed them that they should gather in one area where buses would come to pick them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, these people were not just gathering to pick up buses. They were also detained in the sawmill; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were waiting for buses. That's the information I heard. I didn't hear it from any officials, I heard it from ordinary people in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And from where you were, you didn't see people being brought into the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that area, one could not even see them being brought there because there were buildings obstructing the view. I did see, though, individuals being brought or taken away, not groups though.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that no one was detained in the warehouses of the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not something I can state for a fact, just as I cannot that this was the case, because I didn't see it for myself, but I did hear what I already said, that people were gathering there for that particular reason. And I think that they spent no more than two days there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And from where you were, approximately, as you say, 200 metres away, did you hear any beatings coming from the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you were, as you said earlier before, guarding this building throughout the month of June?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to move to another topic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Hold on a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- because before we leave this issue, Mr. Bubic, did you, at any point, see or hear any buses coming to the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not specifically at the sawmill. I did know of other locations where they were coming but I didn't hear anything of the sort in relation to the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just one last question on this topic: Did you see who was bringing these individuals to the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said a moment ago that I wasn't able to see people as they were brought to the sawmill. I could see individual people being taken out of buildings. As far as I know, those people were taken to the police station. At least that is what soldiers and a policeman who was there told us when we asked them where they were headed with these people. This allegedly because on that day the process of disarming individuals and those who refused to surrender weapons were taken to the police station for interviews. This is the information that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And just to complete this, the police station itself is also not too far from your building, the building you were guarding?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't far, but we were not allowed to leave the area that we guarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Moving on to something you told us on -- yesterday at page 25897. You told us that you learned of a plan to -- by the Croats and the Muslims to organise a hunting lunch on Mount Borje on the 12th of June and they wanted to invite all prominent Serbs. There were lists for liquidation. You told us that yesterday. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that I heard in captivity. Mr. Sprzo himself told me that. I will refrain from the vulgar terms he used in relating this story to me. He was swearing my Chetnik mother and what was said was, "you were lucky because this had been the plan." Truth to tell, I had long been inquiring with my friends of these events in order to arrive at some sort of relevant conclusion, but, to this day, I haven't been successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where I come from, I would ask to strike this answer as non-responsive, but I don't think we'll be doing it here. Sir, the question was: Do you remember what you said yesterday? All you have to say is "Yes, I remember." Can we agree on that? That is what you told the Court yesterday.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: My question was to you: Whether you remember telling us this story yesterday. That's all I asked of you. I want you to focus your answers to my question. You said that to the Court yesterday, yes or no? Yes? Very well. Now --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You don't know if this information is true, do you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right. Now, you told us then when you were released you were debriefed by the military police. This was in July 1992. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not debriefed by the police in July, it was later, because two hours after I was released, I went to Banja Luka for treatment, for medical treatment. So I returned in the first ten days of August. It could have been early August, therefore, that the military police debriefed me. And it was in Banja Luka that I was debriefed, but I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we just pull up tab 16B which is 65 ter 20364.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is a document from the military police in Banja Luka of the 21st of July, 1992. It is an Official Note relating to the events you told us about. If you look at the first paragraph, it says: "Following checks made on the ground, information obtained from the reconnaissance patrols, and interviews conducted with a number of people, and in particular with Obrad Bubic from Kotor Varos, regarding the multiple murders committed on 5 July, the following has been established:" So, sir, does this document refresh your memory, it may have been, in fact, in July? I allow that the passage of time may have affected your memory in that sense, but it appears that you were, in fact, seen in July?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I misunderstood you a moment ago. My understanding was that you had asked me about the debriefing by the military police in Kotor Varos because I wasn't in Kotor Varos at the time, and it is true that I was debriefed in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can put that document away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you were debriefed on that day. You told us that you were also debriefed in Kotor Varos. You provided a signed statement in 1995 and you also published a book in 2004. Now, what seems to me a bit surprising, sir, is that this piece of information that there was a plot to kill prominent Serbs on Mount Borje, which appears to be an important piece of intelligence information, does not appear in any of the documents referring to the events that you went through, not this Official Note, not your book, not your statement in 1995. So what I'd like to ask you is: Did anybody refresh your memory in relation to this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've been aware of this information throughout. Bearing in mind the fact that it was insignificant when it comes to my book where I wrote of my own personal knowledge and suffering, I didn't pay much attention to it and I heard it from people who belonged to the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, your book is about 175 pages and includes a lot of detail. Your statements and your debriefings were given to military police, and this is part of the security organs in the army. Wouldn't you say that this is an important piece of information, the plot to assassinate prominent Serbs in Kotor Varos? This is something that you would have, at the time, informed the military police?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be quite frank, I don't know what moved me not to tell this story, but after all, I was writing about my own golgotha, about my own ordeal and not that of others in the municipality of Kotor Varos. Other than that, I did discuss this issue extensively with my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: But you didn't inform the military police?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't inform anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. On a slightly different topic, sir, when did you arrive in The Hague exactly?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Saturday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Saturday morning. And when did you first meet --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Friday. And when did you first meet with representatives of the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that same day, in the afternoon, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On Friday?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was on the same day in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you meet them again on Saturday?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met up with Mr. Aleksic, and Aleksic, Mr. Krgovic and I had lunch on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This was on Saturday and also on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both on Saturday and Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And on Sunday you had also lunch and dinner with them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be quite frank, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: When you met with them, did you tell them about this event of the 12th of June, or not the events, but what you heard about a plot to assassinate prominent Serbs? Did you tell them at that time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And give or take, can you tell us how many hours you spent with them on Saturday and on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An hour or two, including lunch or dinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That seems like a very short lunch, sir. Did you spend one or two hours each day or in total?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On each of these days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you go through the topics that you would be discussing in court?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, generally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Generally. Were you asked at any point to provide additional clarification on what you had said before to them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, in fact, I did tell Mr. Aleksic not to burden me with these issues overly since I was going to discuss them in court anyway. To be quite honest, I do -- I am at my best if I don't discuss these issues. I feel better. And if I may add, I never re-read the book after I finished writing it. I simply want these things to slip my mind. I don't want to remind myself of these events and misfortunes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And one last question on this topic: Was it on Saturday that you mentioned the issue of the plot to kill prominent Serbs on the 12th of June?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember which day it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was there any day that you just had lunch and dinner and didn't talk about these events at all?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Which day was that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday at page 25926, you told us that Muslims and Croats started moving out of Kotor Varos, that you were present during their departure. Now, when you say moving out, did they move out willingly?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very difficult answer to give. To have anybody move from an area that is their native area is very difficult, but people realise that there was a war on and thought that they would be better off elsewhere. So based on what I know, they asked to leave the area of the municipality of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And these buses were generally convoys going towards Travnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, in September one such convoy was leaving Kotor Varos and heading towards Travnik, and do you remember halting a bus and taking it towards Celinac, towards a school in Celinac to identify people on the bus? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have a recollection but not of that situation. I received an order from the corps command, via my command, that I should be the one to have a look at the column of people leaving Kotor Varos before they boarded buses in the local commune of Zabrdje and that was the only locality where I witnessed this situation. My task was to have a look at these individuals and identify among them those who tortured me, if any of them were, and to see if among them were individuals who used to have weapons and were on the other side. I spent the entire day seeing that column off. Fortunately, I didn't recognise any of the individuals that the military security branch in Banja Luka was interested in. I met quite a few friends that I greeted. I even met a neighbour, a lady neighbour who used to live in my building, Mila or Nena with an odd sounding family name, Zaklan, which means slaughtered in B/C/S, whose husband had died before the war, and I remember seeing this woman who used to be a proper lady and with such demeanour and when I saw her she had two odd pairs of shoes. One was brown and the other black. And I asked her about her sons and she said that she had to leave her elder son back in the woods whereas she was taking the other son along. She told me, "Obrad, Obrad, by God, please give us some bread, if there's any to be found." At that point, a vehicle, driving in the opposite direction from Celinac, appeared. It was a van taking bread to Kotor Varos, and I pulled it over and took a sack with some 12 or 13 breads in it, gave that sack to her, and we parted ways, tearful both of us. And some two or three years ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, sir. I mean, I know that these are very important issues to you, but I must focus your attention, again, to the question. The question was about a bus that you halted and took towards a school in Celinac. Now, these details that you provided us may be of some interest, but I want you to focus, again, your answers to the question. Now, you say you recognised some neighbour of yours, some neighbours of yours in those buses. Now, all of these were Muslims and Croats; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing someone that you recognised by the name of Dzemalija Avdic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately - I was meaning to tell you this - two or three years ago, I came by a book that the Muslims and Croats had published in Zagreb. Among the statements contained in that book there is the statement of Dzemalija Avdic, who used to work with me. He was a plumber in my company. He stated that I was the one who conducted triage of people, selecting those who would be going to the free territory and those who would be sent to Manjaca. The statement that he gave is shameful and I swear by my honour that this is not true. I never did anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you are saying that you never separated a group of men from a group of women and children going towards Travnik? Is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I wasn't separating groups. I didn't separate a single person. And that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And that's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, when was the last time that you saw Stojan Zupljanin before coming to this court?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was during the war, near the very end of the war in Maslovare, as he was taking either his mother or father back from a medical visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you didn't see him after the war?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, when there were rumours in July 1992 that you, too, had been killed in this ambush, is it correct that your brother who lived in Banja Luka called Stojan Zupljanin to go with him to identify what they thought was your body; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And is it correct that your two families were pretty close?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, that's not true. They are not close. We are acquaintances and have been for a very long time, but our lives parted ways, in fact, if I can put it that way. Even when it comes to family visits, we never were on that sort of terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In 1992, what was your brother's occupation in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a driver in the Autoprevoz company in Banja Luka, Holijaz [phoen] company, and he drove the Munich-Banja Luka route all the way until 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So your brother, who was a driver in Banja Luka, was able to get the chief of the Security Services Centre Banja Luka to come with him to identify what was thought to be your body, and you are telling us that your families are not close? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you say families, when you say closeness. I would -- what I would mean by that is we would be socialising, having dinners together, whereas encounters lasting two or three minutes where there would be an exchange of words, well, that's not something that I would consider closeness. Even when it comes to my brother in Banja Luka, I see him once every month or two and I truly never went to visit Stojan, nor did he me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you told us of a number of isolated events in early 1992, the killing of two or three people. However, you didn't tell us when asked questions by Mr. Aleksic any stories about the killings of Muslims, for example, at the medical centre, or the killings of civilians in Vrbanjci, the shelling of Vecici. You did not discuss the arrest of Muslims and Croats in Kotor Varos. Are you telling us that you are not here testifying to help an old friend?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm here to help justice and to contribute towards a reconciliation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I never defended war crime. If anybody committed a war crime, a tribunal is the best place to be judged of that and to punish such persons. So my answer to your question has to be negative, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's all I ask, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very few things, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bubic, when you arrived in The Hague to be proofed for this testimony, did you go and were you seen by a doctor?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
