utterances.text: Just hold on a minute, please. How many times and on what days, if you remember? When did you go to see a physician and why?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I came here, I requested medical escort to this place because in the month of July I contracted a very contagious infectious disease, consumption, Tuberculosis, and I spent the entire month of July and August in hospital. Somebody in the Tribunal, I don't know what service that was, did not grant me medical escort and they told me that they had doctors here who would be able to assist me. I consented to that, and I thanked them for that, they immediately took me to see a doctor, an anaesthesiologist. To my astonishment and to my delight, in a way, the doctor that I saw here in Scheveningen after 20 years managed to establish that I had shrapnel in the body from the bullets that were fired into the car on the day when I was captured. They gave me findings, they gave me X-rays, and so on and so forth. I have quite a lot of problem with some wounds on the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've already heard all that in chief. I think [indiscernible] should control, again, the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bubic, you've already told us all that. On what days, how many times did you go to see the doctor, and how much time did you spend in consultation with the doctor?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you on what days, but I know that I went there three or four times to be examined. I can't remember on what days, unfortunately. I only know that those were lovely people, that they took very good care of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Did you have a back ache on Saturday and did I give you some tablets after previous consultation with the witness and victims service of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's now go back to something entirely different. A lot was said about Mr. Manojlo Tepic, also known as Mane. Some documents were shown to you. Do you remember, if you can tell us, when you were mobilised before you were captured in June? Did you used to meet with Mr. Manojlo Tepic or see him around, and if you did, where was that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Tepic personally but I never met him, not for a single time up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: During that period of time from the 8th of June to the 5th of July, did you ever meet him in the command of the town defence in the place where Captain Stojic was?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up Mr. Bubic's book in e-court again. It is under tab 45. We are looking for page 25 in Serbian and page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on page 48 in Serbian, the left-hand side of the monitor. Can we zoom in on the entire page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bubic, the Prosecutor showed you one part of the page. One part of the page has been translated. However, I would kindly ask you to slowly read for the benefit of the interpreters, to slowly read this page starting with the sentence "truth be told" and read all the way to the penultimate paragraph, but please do it slowly. Be mindful of the interpreters as you read. Aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Truth be told, the names of my tragically perished co-travellers is what I heard in [indiscernible] and I had already forgotten them. He started telling he me about the operation. This is what he called the terrible crime. He was more than satisfied with the success of his combatants. He was not clear how come that I had not been hit with a single bullet. How come that I had remained alive under such heavy infantry fire. To my question -- when asked about what we had talked about along the way, I told them that we had not spoken a word. They were very interested in finding out where they came from, with whom they were and similar. "Sprzo confessed to me then that we suffered the misfortune accidently because the operation was organised for two strong beasts, 'Slobodan Zupljanin and Bosko Peulic,' who to their bad misfortune had not arrived as it had been announced. He spoke very badly about them, characterising them as big war criminals and being deeply convinced that soon an end would come for them, too, considering the fact that they had established a great spy network on our side. He even said that his spies were mostly Serbs who didn't like Slobodan or Peulic, and he was convinced that they were informing him correctly and on a regular basis about their movement. "In passing, he told me that only a minute or two before Savo Tepic had passed by them in a Golf, but, according to him, it was a pity to spoil such a big and well-planned operation just because of one Sava, who they would gladly crucify for that matter, and when he says crucify, obviously he means crucify them like Jesus, of course."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Very well. Based on what you have just read out, and you've testified about that already, who were the targets of the operation, according to what you learned from Sprzo?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Peulic and for Slobodan, they were supposed to be the targets of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Slobodan Zupljanin had been injured, that was a few days before this event, and what do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he had been injured, but I'm not aware of the details of that incident to this very day. I know that he was injured on the road from Vrbanjci to Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Is that the same road that you took on that day?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you, Mr. Bubic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bubic, that brings your testimony to an end. You are now released. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give evidence, especially having regard to the frightening and personally painful experiences that you had, the incident to which you testified. And we trust that you continue to recover from those incidents, albeit 20 years on. So we wish you is a safe journey back to your home. Thank you, sir. The usher would now escort you from the courtroom, because we would not be rising immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- perhaps we better go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment to 9.00 tomorrow morning when the next witness on the Zupljanin list will be called.
